rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Ecological succession ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Ecological succession** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  **Ecological succession** is the predictable, directional change in the species composition of a community over time, ending in a stable **climax community** matched to the climate. It starts from bare rock (primary) or from a disturbed site with soil intact (secondary). The sequence of temporary communities is the **sere**; the first colonisers are **pioneers**.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Definition: gradual, predictable change of species composition culminating in a climax community — 'directional and predictable' are the keywords.  ·  Trick 2: Stages: pioneer → seral stages → climax; hydrarch (water → forest) vs xerarch (bare rock → forest) — both END in mesic climax, the convergence line.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Worked example.** A lava flow cools to bare basalt. Lichens secrete acids, etching the rock and trapping dust — the first soil. Mosses follow, then grasses, then shrubs, then trees; each stage adds organic matter and holds more water, making the site habitable for the next, larger species. Centuries later: forest.…  ·  ## 7. (2) Contrast primary and secondary succession in four points. (3) Compare hydrarch and xerarch seres and note they converge on the same climax. (4) Name the pioneer of xerosere (lichens) and of hydrosere (phytoplankton).…

rows.text: ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Succession is directional community change driven by habitat modification, from pioneer to climax; primary starts without soil and is slow, secondary with soil and is fast; water-started and rock-started seres both end in mesic forest. **Self-check:** can you list five sere stages in order for a bare rock?
